hypothesis: An initial listed-company open-market repurchase announcement may create incremental information or future demand after the first public tradable opportunity; it is not a binding promise to buy all announced shares. No outcome selection by realized completion rate.

historical_population_target.include: All initial repurchase announcements and revisions/cancellations/zero execution records. No selection on subsequent execution, survival or returns.

source_gate: Automatically enumerable fixed-year complete population with request-period reconciliation
Stable event identity and actual original public disclosure datetime in Asia/Taipei
Original initial terms and later corrections kept separate with auditable version chronology
Canceled, unexecuted and delisted issuers not silently excluded
Raw source acquisition, backup/readback, SHA/CRC/manifest verified before downstream analysis

resource_bound.followup: At most one follow-up batch using routes/forms actually discovered in saved official pages; no guessing route permutations, CAPTCHA bypass, insecure TLS or manual downloads. Stop if no usable endpoint is discovered.

returns_protocol_status: Not commissioned. No market outcomes inspected; endpoints, cost, comparison and resource gate must be frozen separately if source gate passes. Existing strategy parameters remain frozen.
disallowed: No backtest or raw price query during source trial
No use of realized buyback completion as an initial feature
No human daily validation or actual orders
Do not represent reused historical years as fresh independent evidence
